From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet dimensioning probe — AtlasAI dedicated sizing

Hi Liam — great to meet last week. To get our sizing right for a Dedicated proposal I put together a short probe so we can align on traffic shape and prompt/response characteristics. Can you take a pass and return this by Wed? If easier, reply inline or drop the sample CSV we discussed.

Key items we need: concurrency and QPS expectations, typical and 95th percentile prompt & response token lengths, percent of requests that use streaming, acceptable p50/p95 latency SLOs, and any burst windows (daily/seasonal).

Questions (short answers work):
1) Typical steady-state RPS and expected peak RPS (please include timezone for peaks).
2) Concurrent open sessions (KV cache reuse) and percent of requests for cached prefixes.
3) Average prompt tokens and average generated tokens at steady-state; 95th token lengths for both.
4) Percent of chats that use streaming vs non-streaming responses.
5) Percent requests that require tool/function calls or multimodal assets (files, images).
6) Target latency p50/p95 (i.e., request-to-first-byte and full response time).
7) Any regulatory constraints (data residency, retention) that would affect private deployment.

Attachment: atlas_example_workload.csv (sample traffic by hour).

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor

From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@atlasai.com>

Cc: Sana Rao <sana@atlasai.com>, ops@atlasai.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet dimensioning probe — AtlasAI dedicated sizing

Grace — thanks, see answers below and attached the filled CSV. Quick note up front: our product is a real-time report generation assistant embedded in dashboards. Most traffic comes from end-user requests that trigger multi-step generations.

1) Steady-state RPS: 8 RPS. Peak RPS: 175 RPS during US-PST business hours (09:00–11:00 PST). We also see weekend micro-peaks ~40% of weekday baseline for some customers.
2) Concurrent open sessions: ~2,300 concurrent sessions (each session keeps a KV for context). Estimated cache reuse: 28% (users often re-run with slight edits).
3) Tokens: Avg prompt tokens 420; avg generated tokens 950. 95th percentile: prompt 1,800 tokens; generated 4,200 tokens.
4) Streaming usage: ~72% of requests use streaming (progressive UI). Non-streaming for batch exports.
5) Tool/multimodal: ~14% of requests call external tools (vector search + DB lookups); 6% include attached CSV/image passed to the model for context.
6) Latency targets: target p50 RTT to first byte 120–200ms; p95 RTT to first byte <700ms. Full response p95 <3.5s is preferred but we can accept progressive streaming.
7) Regulatory: US-only data residency for a subset of customers (we'd prefer a Dedicated cluster in us-west). Retention policy: 30 days for transient logs, longer for anonymized metrics.

Attachment: atlas_workload_filled.csv

Liam

Thanks Liam — this is super helpful. Two follow-ups so we size cache-backed capacity correctly:

• For the ~28% cache reuse, is that uniformly distributed or concentrated in a smaller set of hot sessions? (i.e., top 5% sessions account for X% of cache hits)
• For the streaming requests, are you sending chunk sizes (tokens per chunk) that we should optimize for? Typical chunk size?

If you can send an example of a 95th-percentile conversation (pasted text is fine) that will help our latency modeling. I’ve looped in Rishi to draft a provisional mapping to GPU SKUs.

Best — Grace

On a separate note, we're preparing an initial cost/throughput estimate for Dedicated (monthly committed cores + burst). We should follow up with a quick call this week if you have 30 minutes.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet dimensioning probe — AtlasAI dedicated sizing

Looping in Diego for kernel/mapping details, but quick sizing notes based on Liam's numbers:

• Baseline compute needed: steady-state 8 RPS with avg 1.37k tokens per request (prompt+response) implies ~11k tokens/sec = ~0.27M tokens/minute. Accounting for batching & KV cache (28% reuse) we estimate ~25% token-level savings.
• Peak sizing: 175 RPS * 5.15k avg tokens (95th-case) = ~901k tokens/sec worst-case. We won't provision worst-case 100% of time — plan for burst capacity that can be toggled.
• GPU mapping: Recommend primary SKU nVidia-RTX-A6000-class for steady-state with quantized variants for cost-savings; add a smaller pool of higher-throughput L4/NX GPUs for short peaks and streaming-opt paths.
• Autoscale / warm pools: maintain a warm pool sized for 25–30% of peak to reduce cold-start penalty for KV-heavy sessions.

Next steps: Diego to run a quick perf sweep with a 4k-token generator profile and streaming chunk sizes of 64–128 tokens to validate per-GPU QPS. Also need Atlas to send a sanitized 95th-percentile conversation example.

-rishi
